problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
problems.input_format: First line contains array nums, second line contains integer target.
problems.output_format: Return an array of two integers representing the indices.
problems.constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
Only one valid answer exists.
hints: Try using a hash map to store previously seen values.
Can you solve this in O(n) time?
problems.approach: Iterate through the array and store the complement (target - nums[i]) in a map. If the complement is already in the map, return its index and the current index.

problems.title: Reverse String In-Place
problems.description:
Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters `s`.

You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
hints: Use two pointers: one at the start, one at the end, and swap elements.
problems.approach: Two pointer technique swapping left and right until left >= right.

starter_templates.python:
def reverse_string(s):
    left, right = 0, len(s) - 1
    while left < right:
        s[left], s[right] = s[right], s[left]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return s

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description:
Given a string `s` containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of brackets, and in the correct order.
hints: A stack is the ideal data structure here. Push opening brackets, pop and verify on closing brackets.
problems.approach: Push open brackets into stack. On closing bracket, check top of stack.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer `target`, write a function to search `target` in `nums`. If `target` exists, then return its index. Otherwise, return -1.

You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
problems.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
All integers in nums are unique.
nums is sorted in ascending order.
hints: Use low and high pointers. Calculate mid = low + (high - low) / 2.
problems.approach: Halve the search space on each iteration by comparing the target with nums[mid].

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.

hints: Use sliding window with two pointers and a set or map of visited characters.
problems.approach: Sliding window technique maintaining the last seen index of characters.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`. Merge the two lists into one sorted list and return the head of the new list.
problems.constraints:
The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100
hints: Use a dummy head node to simplify edge cases.
problems.approach: Linear scan comparing nodes of list1 and list2.

problems.title: Second Highest Salary
problems.description: Write a solution to find the second highest distinct salary from the `Employee` table. If there is no second highest salary, return `null`.
problems.constraints: Employee table contains id (PK) and salary (INT).
hints: Use MAX(salary) with a WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee).
problems.approach: Subquery with MAX filter or LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1.

problems.title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
problems.description:
Write a solution to find the employees who earn more than their managers.

Table: Employee (id, name, salary, managerId).
hints: Join the Employee table with itself on e.managerId = m.id.

starter_templates.sql:
SELECT e.name AS Employee
FROM Employee e
JOIN Employee m ON e.managerId = m.id
WHERE e.salary > m.salary;

problems.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.

starter_templates.javascript: function maxSubArray(nums) { let max = nums[0], cur = 0; for (let n of nums) { cur = Math.max(n, cur + n); max = Math.max(max, cur); } return max; }
